overview: Widemouth Bay is a big, sandy beach about three miles south of Bude, facing west into the Atlantic. It’s popular for surfing and swimming, with RNLI lifeguards in summer, several surf schools, and cafés on and around the beach.

The village behind is mostly 20th-century bungalows and holiday homes, with a pub and shops up the hill. This stretch of coast has a long history of smuggling, and south of the bay the coast breaks up into little inlets and coves.

expect.title: Surf
expect.text: A popular surf beach with lessons available from several surf schools.

expect.title: Space
expect.text: A wide beach with plenty of room even in summer.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: Walk south towards the smaller coves, or north to Bude along the clifftops.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About three miles south of Bude.

week.text: A great surf and family beach for a north Cornwall week, with easy parking and cafés. It faces west, so evenings here can be glorious.

pairWith.why: a lively seaside town three miles north

tips: Book a surf lesson ahead in the school holidays.
